overall_simulation_design.objective: Calibrate and validate a single-stage Beer Game supply chain simulator that reproduces inventory, backlog, and pipeline dynamics from observed state-action trajectories and generalizes to out-of-distribution lead times and demand regimes.
overall_simulation_design.initialization: Parse train_data.csv grouped by trajectory_id; for each trajectory read the first row to set initial inventory_0, backlog_0, and pipeline_0 (parse pipeline_items JSON). Infer an initial guess of lead time L0 as the max remaining_lead across early steps. Set random seed from metadata.json. Initialize parameter vector theta with priors/bounds: lead time L (integer), demand model parameters (e.g., Poisson rate or NegBin/AR1), event timing flags (arrival/recording convention), and optional noise terms. During calibration, actions a_t are taken directly from the dataset for each trajectory.
overall_simulation_design.execution: For each candidate parameter vector theta, simulate forward each train trajectory from its initial state using the observed action sequence: at each step process pipeline arrivals per lead-time convention, draw demand d_t from the demand generator parameterized by theta (optionally AR1 on latent demand), fulfill backlog then current demand, update inventory/backlog, update pipeline by decrementing leads and appending a_t at position L. Compute a trajectory discrepancy loss between simulated and observed sequences (weighted errors on inventory, backlog, and pipeline composition/length). Optimize theta via simulation-based inference or gradient-free optimization: (a) ABC-SMC or SNPE to obtain a posterior over theta using summary statistics and the full sequence loss; or (b) point-estimation with CMA-ES/Nelder–Mead with multi-starts and early stopping on within-train temporal holdout. Enforce invariants (nonnegative inventory/backlog, integer pipeline positions) via penalties.
outputs: Calibrated parameter estimates (point estimate or posterior samples) for lead time and demand process
Validation-set evaluation metrics (RMSE/MAE for inventory and backlog; pipeline composition error)
Fitted demand generator object/config and reproducible simulator config (event order, lead convention)
Per-trajectory simulated vs observed traces on validation set and summary plots/tables
OOD scenario stress-test results for altered lead times and/or demand parameters

scale_granularity.population_size: Single agent (retailer node) per trajectory; 100 trajectories per split
scale_granularity.rationale: Dynamics are discrete-period inventory updates with pipeline lead times; no spatial interactions in single-stage Beer Game. One agent suffices because supplier and customer processes are modeled exogenously. The 'day' unit represents the dataset’s discrete period (interpretable as week); metrics are computed per step.

static_attributes: ordering_policy (exogenous playback during calibration; policy parameters for counterfactuals)
agent_archetypes.construction_from_data: For each trajectory, set static trajectory_id and episode_length=61 from metadata.json. Initialize dynamic states from the first row: inventory_0, backlog_0, and pipeline_0 by parsing pipeline_items. Use action sequence a_t from the CSV as exogenous orders during calibration/validation. Initialize lead_time with the max observed remaining_lead as a starting guess; it is then calibrated.
agent_archetypes.update_from_data: During simulation, states update via the transition kernel; data are not directly injected except for actions. The discrepancy between simulated and observed (inventory, backlog, pipeline) drives parameter updates in the optimizer/SBI. Optionally, implied demand per step can be reconstructed from observed state differences and used as summary statistics for SBI.

interaction_topology.construction_from_data: supplier_interface: pipeline update rules inferred from pipeline_items (decrement positions; arrivals when remaining_lead threshold met; append orders at position L). customer_interface: demand is latent and modeled probabilistically; its parameters are calibrated to match observed state transitions. No explicit multi-agent edges are required.

exogenous_signals.name: action_stream
exogenous_signals.construction_from_data: action column per (trajectory_id, time_step) from train/val/test CSVs
exogenous_signals.observability: Retailer observes and executes; no delay/noise (playback during calibration/validation)
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Appended to pipeline at position L each step
exogenous_signals.bounds: [0, 10] (dataset shows constant 4; allow headroom for counterfactuals)

exogenous_signals.name: latent_demand
exogenous_signals.construction_from_data: Not observed; inferred via calibration using observed state transitions and pipeline arrivals
exogenous_signals.observability: Unobserved by the model at calibration time; realized as stochastic draw during simulation
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Consumes available inventory; unmet portion increases backlog
exogenous_signals.bounds: [0, 50] per step; governed by calibrated demand parameters

exogenous_signals.name: time_index
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Optional seasonality/trend feature in demand model or policy

Retailer.policy_form: Calibration/validation uses action playback (a_t from data). For counterfactual/generalization, use a base-stock policy with optional demand-forecast smoothing: a_t = clip(0, A_max, S - (inventory_t + on_order_t) + k*backlog_t + forecast_t), where forecast_t = alpha * d_{t-1} + (1-alpha) * forecast_{t-1}; orders are appended at position L.

holdout_plan.train_range: For each training trajectory: steps t=0–48 (first ~80% of 61 steps) for objective accumulation; also use full train split for final fit.
holdout_plan.validation_range: For each training trajectory: steps t=49–60 for early stopping/tuning; primary evaluation on the provided val_data.csv (all steps). Test_data.csv reserved for final OOD checks.
holdout_plan.notes: Primary calibration is on train_data.csv using full sequences; within-trajectory temporal holdout can guide early stopping or hyperparameter selection. Validation metrics reported on val_data.csv with actions fixed to observed.

metrics.name: RMSE_inventory
metrics.definition: Root mean squared error between simulated and observed inventory over time and trajectories

metrics.name: RMSE_backlog
metrics.definition: Root mean squared error between simulated and observed backlog

metrics.name: MAE_pipeline_len
metrics.definition: Mean absolute error of pipeline_len per step

metrics.name: PipelineComp_L1
metrics.definition: Average L1 distance between simulated and observed pipeline occupancy vectors across positions 1..L (sum of absolute differences in quantities by remaining lead)

metrics.name: DemandNLL (optional)
metrics.definition: Negative log-likelihood of reconstructed implied demand under the calibrated demand model (if using likelihood-based fitting)

simulation_evaluation.comparison_method: For each validation trajectory, initialize simulator from the first row, play back observed actions, and simulate with calibrated parameters. Compute metrics per trajectory and aggregate (mean, std, and 95% CI across trajectories). Report tables for aggregate metrics and per-trajectory distributions; optionally provide time-series plots of observed vs simulated means with bands.

calibratable_parameters.name: lead_time_L
calibratable_parameters.source: Constrained by observed max remaining_lead in pipeline_items; initialized at observed max (often 2).
calibratable_parameters.notes: Integer; controls pipeline positions and arrival timing.

calibratable_parameters.name: arrival_convention
calibratable_parameters.source: Event-order ambiguity between datasets and simulators.
calibratable_parameters.notes: Discrete flag; can be optimized via grid search nested in outer optimizer.

calibratable_parameters.name: demand_family
calibratable_parameters.source: Model selection via AIC/BIC on implied demand or via ABC model probabilities.
calibratable_parameters.notes: Choose one family; others can be compared via validation fit.

calibratable_parameters.name: poisson_lambda
calibratable_parameters.source: If demand_family=Poisson; seeded by mean implied demand from train.

calibratable_parameters.name: negbin_r
calibratable_parameters.notes: Controls overdispersion; pair with p or mean/var parameterization.

calibratable_parameters.name: negbin_p
calibratable_parameters.notes: Alternative parameterization to match mean/variance of implied demand.

calibratable_parameters.name: ar1_mu
calibratable_parameters.source: If demand_family=AR1-Normal on latent demand; unconditional mean.
calibratable_parameters.notes: Works with truncation at 0 if mapping to nonnegative demand.

calibratable_parameters.name: ar1_sigma
calibratable_parameters.notes: Maps to demand via max(0, round(latent)).

calibratable_parameters.name: seasonal_amplitude
calibratable_parameters.source: Optional deterministic seasonality on demand using time_index.
calibratable_parameters.notes: Use with seasonal_period; set to 0 if not needed.

calibratable_parameters.name: seasonal_period
calibratable_parameters.source: Optional; integer period for seasonality component.

calibratable_parameters.name: inventory_obs_noise_sigma
calibratable_parameters.source: Allows small measurement mismatch between simulator and data.
calibratable_parameters.notes: Penalized toward 0 to avoid absorbing structural errors.

calibratable_parameters.name: initial_state_noise_sigma
calibratable_parameters.source: Randomization around observed initial inventory/backlog for robustness.
calibratable_parameters.notes: Used only during calibration robustness checks; set to 0 for final fit.

calibratable_parameters.name: policy_S
calibratable_parameters.notes: Not used during playback-based calibration; used for OOD policy experiments.

calibratable_parameters.name: policy_k
calibratable_parameters.source: Backlog urgency weight in base-stock policy.

calibratable_parameters.name: policy_alpha
calibratable_parameters.source: EWMA smoothing for demand forecast in policy.

calibratable_parameters.name: A_max
calibratable_parameters.notes: Set >= observed max action; playback ignores.
